newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia PM says mulls action against speculators.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM says mulls action against speculators.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad pressed ahead with criticisms of "rogue speculators" on Monday, saying his government would consider taking punitive actions against them.

"What we can do depends on our perception. If we perceive this as a criminal act, then we will act. If you think that it's normal, then you don't act," the national Bernama news agency quoted the prime minister as telling reporters.
Mahathir did not specify the measures Malaysia might take.

"The government has got some ideas on what to do but obviously we cannot just publish what we want to do...," he said in repines to questions after receiving foreign ministers here for meetings of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
In the past week, Mahathir has castigated currency speculators, whom he blames for seeking to undermine Southeast Asia's economies.
His tirade reached fever pitch on Wednesday, when he told the 30th ministerial meetings of ASEAN he considered such speculators "anarchists", "rogues" and "international manipulators".
Malaysia and neighbouring countries have seen heavy attacks on their currencies in the past month, forcing devaluations in Thailand and the Philippines and expensive intervention efforts in Malaysia.
Singapore and Indonesia have also had to stave off sharp selling in their currencies.

ASEAN has expressed serious concerns over the situation, saying in its closing ministerial meeting statement on Friday that it saw "well coordinated efforts to destabilise ASEAN currencies for self serving purposes".
But the nine-member regional grouping did not propose any concrete solutions or laws except for a tightening of ASEAN cooperation to combat the problem.
Mahathir said the currency issue was discussed in his meeting with ASEAN's 10 so-called dialogue partners of Asian and Western powers.
He said some of the partners suggested the matter be raised at the 18-member Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Forum in Vancouver in November.
Asked whether he would do so, Mahathir said: "I don't know whether we can raise this thing," Bernama reported.
